critical_code_review_comments: reels.tsx:25 — Dimensions.get('window') is captured at module load; on web preview this can differ from the current viewport (measured height=1080 vs viewport 844). On a real device this is fine, but if we ever need pixel-accurate web-preview parity, switch to `useWindowDimensions()` and derive reelHeight in-component. The current fix (reelHeight = SCREEN_H, snapToInterval == reelHeight) is still correct because both values come from the same source, so no gap/overlap between snapped items regardless of the numeric value.

reels.tsx:145,172 — actions and bottom info use `bottom: tabBarSpace + 16` and `tabBarSpace + 12`. tabBarSpace = 66 + max(insets.bottom,8) + 16 = ~90 on iOS. That correctly positions the pills above the floating pill bar without hugging the reel edge. Good.

_layout.tsx:79-130 — custom `tabBar` prop is well-implemented: uses navigation.emit('tabPress') with canPreventDefault (so tab-press interceptors still work) and falls back to navigate() only if not defaultPrevented. This is the correct expo-router / react-navigation contract.
_layout.tsx:190-203 — CreateFab uses LinearGradient (#FF8C66→#FF6B3D) at 52x44 with 16 radius, elevation 8 and orange shadow. Distinct-from-IG ✓.

discover.tsx / home.tsx / ProfileView.tsx — paddingBottom set to `110 + insets.bottom` across all FlatLists so the last row/card clears the floating 66px pill bar + 8px bottom offset + 16 gap ≈ 90+16=106 → 110 has a small safety margin. Verified via scroll to end on Home feed on web preview.
reels.tsx uses `expo-video`'s VideoView + useVideoPlayer (NOT the deprecated `expo-av`). ✓

rca_of_issue: Original user bug (reels overlap): the previous reels.tsx computed `reelHeight = SCREEN_H - tabBarSpace` while the FlatList still occupied SCREEN_H and used `snapToInterval={reelHeight}`. Because snapToInterval was smaller than the visible viewport, each snap advanced by less than a full screen, so the top of the next reel bled into the tab-bar-sized gap below the current reel → the 'I can still see the video above' strip. Fix: set `reelHeight = SCREEN_H` so snapToInterval equals the viewport height; the floating tab bar now correctly overlays the reel gradient at the bottom (standard Reels/TikTok pattern) and there is exactly zero gap between snapped items. Verified via DOM measurement: reels are 1080px tall each, snapToInterval=1080, and after scrollTop=1080 the second reel's top is 0 exactly (previous reel bottom = 0 exactly). Reproduction step-through and mitigation: any change in the future that reintroduces `SCREEN_H - <something>` for reelHeight while keeping the FlatList at SCREEN_H will bring the bug back — the invariant is `FlatList.height === reelHeight === snapToInterval`.
